description: The bar chart visually compares the average attention distribution across three input segments—Context, Generated Response, and Other—during text generation for two model variants: “Ours” and “Standard.” The vertical axis lists the two model categories, while the horizontal axis represents percentage values ranging from 0% to 100%, with no explicit tick marks but implied by the segmented bar lengths. Each horizontal bar is segmented into three colored portions: blue (Context), orange (Generated Response), and green (Other), as indicated by the legend below. For the “Ours” model, attention is distributed as 60.6% to Context (blue), 31.7% to Generated Response (orange), and 7.7% to Other (green). In contrast, the “Standard” model allocates 23.6% to Context (blue), 51.1% to Generated Response (orange), and 25.3% to Other (green). The bars are not sorted by magnitude but are grouped by model type, with “Ours” positioned above “Standard.” The visual contrast highlights that “Ours” heavily favors Context, while “Standard” shifts attention toward Generated Response and Other, with the latter nearly quadrupling in proportion compared to “Ours.” No bars are shaded, outlined, or annotated beyond their percentage labels, and the chart uses a clean, segmented bar format to emphasize proportional differences between the two models without additional graphical embellishments.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the average rate at which the model attends most to each input segment: context, generated response, or other (e.g., system prompts) during generation. The vertical axis contains the categories labeled 'Ours' and 'Standard,' while the horizontal axis represents the percentage composition. Each bar is divided into three segments, with colors representing different categories: blue for 'Context,' orange for 'Generated Response,' and green for 'Other.' The 'Ours' bar is composed of approximately 60.6% Context (blue), 31.7% Generated Response (orange), and 7.7% Other (green). The 'Standard' bar consists of approximately 23.6% Context (blue), 41.1% Generated Response (orange), and 35.3% Other (green). Notably, the 'Standard' model demonstrates a significant decline in attention to Context compared to the 'Ours' model, while the attention to Other increases substantially. This suggests that the 'Standard' model prioritizes system prompts over contextual information during generation.
